request.system_prompt:
You are the defect reviewer agent of LANSH, a factory that migrates legacy SAS 9.4 jobs to PySpark. LANSH reproduces every legacy behaviour exactly, bugs included, and asks a person to decide what to do about each suspected bug, so finding them matters.

Read the job and list the places where the code most likely does not do what its author intended: wrong comparisons or boundaries, joins that multiply rows, gaps or overlaps in bands, wrong date columns, missing values handled wrongly, truncation, hard-coded constants that should vary. Ignore style, performance and things that are merely unusual. For each, write one Spark SQL SELECT over the views listed that measures the impact on the legacy output: it must return exactly one row with rows_affected (the output rows the bug changes) and, when the bug changes an amount, amount_affected (the total change, positive). Compare what the legacy output holds with what the intended logic would give. Use only the views and columns listed.

defects.description: The macro is called with a fixed list (MOT HOM TRV) and only those three score tables are unioned. Customer/line rows in claims_enriched with any other lob_code, including a differently cased or null code, never reach rpt.risk_scores. Their claims still count towards the line loss ratios.
defects.impact_query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM(ABS(COALESCE(paid,0))),0) AS amount_affected FROM (SELECT customer_id, lob_code, SUM(total_paid) AS paid FROM dw_claims_enriched WHERE lob_code IS NULL OR lob_code NOT IN ('MOT','HOM','TRV') GROUP BY customer_id, lob_code) x
defects.intended_behaviour: Score every line of business in the claims experience, with the list built from the data (e.g. select distinct lob_code into a macro variable) instead of hard-coded.
defects.title: Hard-coded line-of-business list drops other lines

defects.description: Points and score are built with + and *, which pass missing values through. If n_recoveries is missing (every claim has null n_recoveries), loss_ratio is missing (the line has no row in premium_band_summary because of the inner join in lob_ratio), or age_load/county_load are missing (the customer is not in dim_customer, through the left join), then points and score come out missing. The tier IF chain then sends a missing score to 'LOW'. The author clearly wanted a default for missing values (a missing age gets age_load 1.00 on line 25), but unmatched customers and missing components get no default.
defects.impact_query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM(ROUND((12.5*LEAST(n_claims,4) + 7.5*COALESCE(n_recoveries,0) + CASE WHEN severity >= 2 THEN 10 WHEN severity >= 1 THEN 5 ELSE 0 END + COALESCE(ROUND(5*loss_ratio)/2,0)) * COALESCE(age_load,1) * COALESCE(county_load,1), 2)),0) AS amount_affected FROM golden_rpt_risk_scores WHERE score IS NULL
defects.intended_behaviour: Default missing components to neutral values: recoveries 0, lob_points 0, loads 1.00. Then compute a real score and tier, or flag the row explicitly instead of quietly putting it in LOW.
defects.title: Missing inputs make the score missing and silently tier the row LOW

defects.description: work.cust takes every row of dw.dim_customer with no filter for the current version. The dimension has version_count/_row_seq columns, which suggests it keeps history. The left join on customer_id then repeats each customer/line score row once per customer version, and ages or counties can differ between versions.
defects.impact_query: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(n-1),0) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM(ABS(COALESCE(paid,0))*(n-1)),0) AS amount_affected FROM (SELECT customer_id, lob_code, COUNT(*) AS n, MAX(paid) AS paid FROM golden_rpt_risk_scores GROUP BY customer_id, lob_code HAVING COUNT(*) > 1) d
defects.intended_behaviour: Join exactly one (current) customer record per customer_id, so there is one output row per customer and line.
defects.title: Customer dimension join can multiply score rows

defects.description: Age is int((as_of - date_of_birth)/365.25). This understates the age of people whose birthday falls on or just before the reporting date (e.g. born 2000-12-31 gives 24, not 25 at 2025-12-31). That can move them across the 25 or 70 loading boundaries.
defects.impact_query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected FROM golden_rpt_risk_scores g WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dw_dim_customer c WHERE CAST(c.customer_id AS DOUBLE) = g.customer_id AND c.date_of_birth IS NOT NULL AND (2025 - YEAR(c.date_of_birth)) <> g.age)
defects.intended_behaviour: Use the exact completed age at the reporting date (e.g. intck('year', date_of_birth, &as_of, 'c')). At 2025-12-31 this is 2025 - year(date_of_birth).
defects.title: Age approximated by days/365.25

defects.description: as_of is used only for age. Claims, payments and recoveries are taken from claims_enriched whatever their loss or reported date, so claims after the reporting date add to counts, paid, severity and loss ratio.
defects.impact_query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM(ABS(COALESCE(paid,0))),0) AS amount_affected FROM (SELECT customer_id, lob_code, SUM(total_paid) AS paid FROM dw_claims_enriched WHERE lob_code IN ('MOT','HOM','TRV') AND (loss_date > DATE'2025-12-31' OR reported_date > DATE'2025-12-31') GROUP BY customer_id, lob_code) x
defects.intended_behaviour: Keep only claims with loss_date (or reported_date) on or before &as_of.
defects.title: Claims experience not limited to the reporting date
